adjudications.reason: Anchors the document-level adversarial lens: premise challenge, assumption surfacing, decision stress-testing, simplification pressure, and alternative blindness, with depth calibrated to document size and stakes.

Anchors the code-level adversarial lens. Its framing — construct the failure rather than check against criteria — and its calibration of depth by diff size and risk domain are the charter shape the whole set is modelled on.

Reviews parity between a user-facing interface and an agent-facing one. A repository with neither surface has no subject for this lens, and the parity rule is a product decision an adopter makes, not a default the product should assert.
Authors documentation to a named individual's template. It reviews nothing, and it is person-named as well.
Anchors the contract lens: breaking changes to a published surface, missing versioning or migration path, divergent failure shapes, and silent semantic drift.
Anchors the architecture lens: placement, dependency direction, boundary erosion, and the long-term cost of decisions that are expensive to reverse.
Gathers external conventions and guidance. It produces input to a decision rather than a judgement about a candidate.

Reviews command-line surfaces against a readiness rubric. Repositories that ship no command-line surface have no subject, and the rubric is a second grading mechanism beside the shipped severity vocabulary.
The diff-triggered variant of the same command-line readiness lens; excluded for the same reason.
Anchors the simplicity lens as a final pass: the subtraction test, generality without a second consumer, and the smallest version that would have worked.
Anchors the document-consistency lens: contradiction, counts that disagree with their contents, unresolvable references, terminology drift, and ambiguity that would split implementers.
Anchors the mandatory outcome-correctness lens: boundaries, absent values, ordering and interleaving, invalid state transitions, and broken failure propagation.

Anchors the durable-data lens: irreversible transformations, transitions that assume a quiet system, constraints that do not hold, partial writes, dangling relationships, and sensitive values in the wrong place.

Validates migrations against a specific storage technology and its query language. Its transferable substance — irreversible transformation and partial application — is already carried by persona.data-integrity.
The diff-triggered variant of the same storage-specific migration lens; its transferable substance is carried by persona.data-integrity.
Produces a release checklist with queries, rollback steps, and monitoring plans. It directs an operational procedure rather than judging a candidate.
Compares a rendered interface against a design held in a specific external design tool. The tool dependency is precisely the per-host binding the set forbids.
Runs repeated change-and-inspect cycles to improve an interface. It performs work rather than reviewing it.

The genuine borderline case, decided against inclusion. It reviews planning documents for missing interface decisions — information architecture, interaction states, user flows — which presupposes a human-facing product surface. A general delivery product installs into libraries, services, and command-line tools where the lens has no subject at all, so shipping it by default would activate a lens most adopters cannot satisfy. Its dimensional rating rubric is also a second grading mechanism beside the shipped severity vocabulary. An adopter with an interface surface can supply it as a repository-owned charter at a protected path, which the policy layer already resolves by identity and digest.
Encodes a named individual's opinions, and is bound to a single web framework as well.
Anchors the feasibility lens: conflicts with what exists, missing dependencies, ordering that cannot hold, and transitions with no path from the deployed shape to the proposed one.
Detects and applies visual differences against a specific external design tool. It edits rather than reviews, and is tool-bound as well.
Gathers documentation for a dependency. It produces reference material, not a judgement.
Traces how code came to be as it is. Useful context for a reviewer; not itself a review bar.
Summarises reported problems across a tracker. It analyses a corpus rather than judging a candidate, and depends on a specific tracker surface.

Encodes a named individual's opinions, and is bound to specific front-end libraries. Its transferable substance — ordering and interleaving faults — is carried by persona.outcome-correctness and persona.adversarial.
Encodes a named individual's bar for one language.
Encodes a named individual's bar for one web framework.
Encodes a named individual's bar for one language.
Searches recorded past learnings for applicable prior art. It supplies context before work rather than judging a candidate after it.
Anchors the maintainability lens: premature abstraction, unnecessary indirection, dead code, coupling without a reason in the domain, and names that obscure intent.

Covers pattern and anti-pattern consistency and duplication, which is the maintainability lens seen from the other side. Folded in as the duplication-that-will-drift and naming clauses rather than shipped as a near-duplicate persona.
Covers algorithmic complexity, memory, and scalability alongside the same query and hot-path concerns. Folded into the single performance charter as its complexity-class and unbounded-growth clauses.

Anchors the performance lens: repeated lookups inside a loop, unbounded growth, missing limits at a boundary, hot-path work that could be done once, and blocking work where the caller cannot afford it.
Assesses existing review threads and implements fixes. It acts on review output rather than producing it, and depends on a hosting platform's thread surface.

Checks whether prior feedback was addressed, which requires a hosting platform's review-thread surface. The general property it protects — that a repair round actually repaired what was raised — belongs to the delivery loop's own review-round reduction, not to a shipped charter.
Anchors the product lens: premise challenge before solution, and strategic consequences across trajectory, positioning, adoption, opportunity cost, and compounding direction.

Anchors the standards lens, and is the one lens whose criteria are the adopting repository's own written rules rather than anything the product ships. The charter carries the discipline — cite the rule or do not file — without carrying any specific repository's rules.
Anchors the reliability lens: unhandled failure at a boundary, retries without a ceiling, missing deadlines, swallowed failures, cascades, and partial work left behind.
Researches a repository's structure and conventions for someone about to work in it. It orients rather than judges.
Cross-references a generated schema artifact specific to one framework's migration tooling.
Anchors the scope lens: what already exists, the minimum change set, work serving no stated goal, abstractions ahead of consumers, and priority that does not order.
Covers security at the planning-document level. Folded into the single security charter as its design-level clause, so one identity serves the lens whether the subject is code or a plan.

Anchors the security lens: traced injection paths, authentication and authorization gaps, secrets, unsafe decoding, outbound requests and path handling, and its deliberately lower threshold with the residual-risk discipline that keeps that from becoming speculation.

Covers the same territory as a standing audit rather than a diff-scoped review. Its transferable substance is folded into the single security charter; its checklist framing is deliberately not carried, because the charter reviews the delivered subject rather than auditing the repository.
Searches prior working sessions for context. It supplies history, and it enumerates specific host products by name, which the set forbids.
Searches a specific messaging product for organizational context. It gathers rather than judges, and is tool-bound as well.

Analyses a specification for flow completeness and gaps, which is the coherence lens applied to described sequences. Folded in as the completeness-of-described-flows clause rather than shipped as a near-duplicate persona.
Reviews one language and one mobile platform's project, entitlement, and signing artifacts.

Anchors the mandatory testing-policy lens: untested branches, assertions that prove nothing, rows coupled to implementation, missing failure-path coverage, and behavioural change with no test movement.
Performs external research and returns grounding material. It informs work rather than judging it.

dispositions.adapted: This file is the primary basis for one shipped charter. Its substance is rewritten as host- and stack-neutral charter prose; its agent frontmatter and host bindings are not carried over.
dispositions.excluded: This file does not ship. The exclusionRule states which rule decided it.
dispositions.merged: This file covers a lens another file already anchors. Its substance is folded into that charter rather than shipped as a near-duplicate persona.

exclusionRules.not-a-reviewer: The file directs research, authoring, synthesis, or another action rather than reviewing a delivery candidate against a bar. A charter that tells a reviewer to go and do something is a second source of orchestration authority, which the persona set must not carry.
exclusionRules.person-named: The file encodes a named individual's taste. A general product ships lens categories, not personalities.
exclusionRules.stack-bound: The file is written against a specific language, framework, or storage technology. Shipping it would import one adopter's stack into a set that must stay neutral.
exclusionRules.surface-bound: The file presupposes a product surface that a large fraction of adopting repositories do not have.
exclusionRules.tool-bound: The file depends on a specific external tool or hosting platform surface, which is exactly the per-host binding the persona set forbids.

purpose: One recorded include/exclude decision, with a reason, for every reviewer-agent source file considered as a basis for the shipped reviewer charter set. The exclusions are the substantive claim: without this record a later persona release would silently re-litigate the same calls.
